title: The Future Indicative
subtitle: λύσω — action that will happen.
objectives: Conjugate any regular ω-verb in the future indicative active and middle.
Recognize the sigma as the marker of the future tense.
Understand the contracted future of liquid verbs (μενῶ, ἀρῶ).
Translate future forms correctly in context.

sections.heading: The future tense
sections.body:
The future expresses action that will happen. λύσω means 'I will loose'. The future tense is formed by inserting a sigma (σ) between the verb stem and the endings. The endings are the same as the present, but with the sigma infix.

The future has no augment. The augment marks past time; the future is not past.

The future middle is common. λύσομαι means 'I will free myself' or 'I will free (for myself)'. The future passive has separate forms (λυθήσομαι), which you will learn in Stage 4.

sections.heading: The future indicative active: λύσω
sections.body:
singular
  1st   λύσω        I will loose
  2nd   λύσεις      you will loose
  3rd   λύσει       he/she/it will loose

  plural
  1st   λύσομεν     we will loose
  2nd   λύσετε      you (plural) will loose
  3rd   λύσουσι(ν)  they will loose

The sigma is the marker. The thematic vowel is ο/ε as usual.

sections.heading: The future indicative middle: λύσομαι
sections.body:
singular
  1st   λύσομαι     I will free myself
  2nd   λύσῃ        you will free yourself
  3rd   λύσεται     he/she/it will free himself/herself/itself

  plural
  1st   λυσόμεθα    we will free ourselves
  2nd   λύσεσθε     you (plural) will free yourselves
  3rd   λύσονται    they will free themselves

sections.heading: The contracted future: liquid verbs
sections.body:
Verbs whose stems end in λ, ρ, μ, or ν (the liquids) do not add σ directly. Instead, the σ drops and the vowel contracts.

μένω (I remain) → μενέω → μενῶ (I will remain)
αἴρω (I lift) → ἀρέω → ἀρῶ (I will lift)

The contraction follows predictable rules. For now, just recognize that liquid-stem verbs have contracted futures without the visible σ.

items.prompt: First person singular future active of λύω
Third person singular future active of λύω
First person singular future middle of λύω
What is the marker of the future tense?
items.answer: The sigma (σ) between the stem and the ending.

items.prompt: Do liquid verbs have a visible σ in the future?
items.answer: No, the σ drops and the vowel contracts.

words.gloss: We will remain in the city.

sections.heading: Up next
sections.body: Lesson 3.5 introduces the first aorist. The aorist is the basic past tense for completed action. ἔλυσα means 'I loosed' (simple past). The aorist uses the augment ἐ- and the sigma infix, with a new set of endings.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark the lesson complete when you can conjugate the future active and middle of any ω-verb from memory and can translate future forms correctly.
